lesson.title: Technological Advances and Limitations After 1900: Disease
lesson.summary: How medicine defeated some diseases while poverty-related diseases persisted and new epidemics emerged.
learningGoals: Explain how disease and medical advances affected people from 1900 to the present.
lesson.bigIdea: Medicine won great victories after 1900, but diseases of poverty persisted, new epidemics spread quickly in a connected world, and longer lives brought new illnesses.
lesson.context: The same air travel and trade that connected the world also let diseases spread farther and faster.

sections.title: Old and new epidemics

blocks.text: The influenza pandemic of 1918 to 1919, a worldwide outbreak spread partly by soldiers returning from World War I, killed tens of millions. HIV/AIDS, identified in the early 1980s, spread worldwide and hit sub-Saharan Africa hardest. Ebola in West Africa from 2014 and COVID-19 from 2020 showed how fast disease could cross borders.
Diseases associated with poverty, such as malaria, tuberculosis, and cholera, continued to kill millions, especially where clean water and health care were scarce.

blocks.title: Cause and effect
blocks.text: Global travel spread new diseases faster, while poverty limited access to clean water, vaccines, and treatment.

sections.takeaway: New epidemics spread quickly in a connected world, and diseases of poverty persisted.

sections.title: Medical advances and longer lives

blocks.text: Vaccines prevented polio and measles, and a World Health Organization campaign eradicated smallpox by 1980. Drugs that slowed HIV turned it from a death sentence into a manageable illness for those who could get treatment.
As life expectancy rose, more people lived long enough to develop heart disease, cancer, and Alzheimer's disease, which became leading causes of death in wealthier countries.

blocks.title: Common trap
blocks.text: Medical progress did not reach everyone at the same time. In 2003, only a small share of Africans with HIV received the drugs that were already common in wealthy countries.

sections.takeaway: Medicine lengthened lives, which changed which diseases were most common.

connections.title: Disease and connection
connections.body: Smallpox crossed the Atlantic with the Columbian Exchange; in the twentieth century, a global campaign eradicated it.
connections.transferQuestion: How did global connections both spread and help defeat disease?
